official_sources.supports: DHA's published OVS onboarding channel and public-sector/private-sector verification service context.
Later official statement concerning OVS access and fees.

established_facts: OVS is a server-side register-verification route for authorized/registered third parties.
Publicly published onboarding contact is Verifications@dha.gov.za.
Access is not granted by the existence of a public contact address.
unresolved_questions: Eligibility and legal basis for the specific Luminous Dynamics use case.
Current approved technical contract, authentication, schemas, error codes, limits and test environment.
Permitted fields, purposes, retention, onward-use restrictions, fees and incident procedures.

official_sources.supports: Official announcement and live demonstration of a working smartphone-bound Digital ID prototype on 1 October 2026.
Draft Digital Identity regulations and public-comment process.
Published Digital Identity/PKI programme targets and medium-term planning context.

established_facts: DHA publicly announced a working prototype credential issued through the Population Register and bound to a smartphone chip.
The reviewed public material does not establish a Mycelix-ready external relying-party protocol.
unresolved_questions: Official credential format, verification protocol and exact supported version.
Issuer trust metadata, key rotation, holder binding, expiry and status/revocation methods.
Verifier eligibility, authorization, sandbox, conformance programme, fees and operational support.
Final applicable regulations and exact privacy/consent boundaries.

official_sources.supports: Institutional onboarding steps, required documentation and contract requirement for access to NIA's Identity Verification System Platform.
NIA notice stating L.I. 2523 took effect on 9 June 2026 and explains biometric-verification and card-copy restrictions.

established_facts: NIA describes an institutional identity-verification service with formal onboarding and a signed contract required before access.
The published onboarding checklist includes legal authority for data collection, data-protection certification and requested data needs.
NIA's 2026 notice restricts visual-only verification and copying/retention of Ghana Card copies except where legally permitted.
unresolved_questions: Whether this proposed applicant and specific use case qualify for NIA onboarding.
Current official protocol/API schema, sandbox and conformance procedure for an eligible relying party.
Applicable lawful purpose, permitted fields, biometric handling, retention and redress requirements for the proposed service.

official_sources.supports: NIDA's official announcement of its new Digital ID programme.
Official service guidance describing digital/physical ID forms and biometric collection.

established_facts: NIDA publicly announced a national e-ID programme.
Official service guidance describes digital and physical credential forms and collection of sensitive biometric data.
unresolved_questions: External relying-party authorization, API/protocol documentation and sandbox access.
Issuer trust metadata, status lifecycle, key management and permitted claim scopes.
Cross-border data transfer rules, controller responsibilities, correction/appeal procedures and non-biometric alternatives.

route_records.route_name: National Identification Number (NIN) / digital trust ecosystem

official_sources.supports: NIMC's 26 June 2026 announcement about the NIMC Act 2026, including the Commission's reported PKI/DPI role.

established_facts: NIMC announced the signing of the NIMC Act 2026 and described new roles in national PKI/DPI and interoperable data exchange.
unresolved_questions: Independent legal review of the enacted Act, regulations and implementing instruments.
Official external-verifier protocol, trust metadata, sandbox, eligibility and written authorization.
Scope limits, purpose/legal basis, retention, appeal, breach response and country-specific conformance criteria.

notes: This is a research matrix, not an integration registry. Every route is research_only and production_enabled=false.
Official programme announcements and national service portals establish only the claims explicitly listed; they do not demonstrate that Mycelix has access or permission.
The matrix deliberately separates the South African OVS and smartphone Digital ID routes.
Protocol, authorization, trust metadata and release review remain unconfirmed for all listed routes as of the snapshot date.
A route may advance only with evidence tied to an exact source/version and written authorization from the responsible authority.
No real identity data was processed, and no government endpoint was contacted as part of this research.
